properties.name: seam_report ran against real pairs for the first time — 5 paired, 0 conflicts, and 30 of 40 axes stated by NOBODY
properties.statement:
MEASURED 2026-08-21, at Anthony's direction, against dynograph-foundation's committed export (179 nodes, written by reflow2 0.16.0, unchanged since 2026-07-27). This is THE HALF `dec:linked-repos-poc` COULD NOT REACH on 2026-08-06 and has sat `proposed` for two weeks waiting for.

=== THE POC'S OWN PREDICTION HELD, EXACTLY ===

Its closing line: "THE CHEAPEST NEXT STEP, NOT TAKEN HERE: declare reflow2's `required` interfaces... It would convert 15 dead surfaces into real pairs or real unmet needs." That step was taken since. Re-running the same pairing today:

  2026-08-06   paired 0    dead_surface 15   unmet_needs 0    seam_findings 0
  2026-08-21   paired 5    dead_surface  1   unmet_needs 3    seam_report RAN

All five pair at name_score 100/100 and agree on medium: req-dyno-core-api<->core-api, graph-api, resolution-api, storage-api, vector-api. The three unmet needs are correct and none is dynograph's to publish — the ambient agent, an exclusive local block device, the MCP protocol. The one dead surface is `ifc:rest-v1`, dynograph's 80-operation HTTP API, which reflow2 genuinely does not consume.

=== WHAT seam_report ACTUALLY SAID, AND IT IS NOT "COMPATIBLE" ===

  pairs_checked 5 | agreed 10 axes | differs 0 | incompatible 0 | UNSTATED 30

Its own words: "an unstated axis is not an agreed one, and this is not a claim of compatibility." So the seam between reflow2 and dynograph-foundation is **75% UNDESCRIBED**, not 75% agreed. Both sides stated `medium: library` and almost nothing else — no payload_schema, no error_model, no operations on reflow2's side of any pair.

⇒ THE ANSWER IS A GOOD ONE AND THE NUMBER LOOKS LIKE A PASS. `incompatible: 0` beside `unstated: 30` is the same shape as the PoC's own warning about `unmet_needs: 0` — a zero that reads as health and means nobody said anything. The tool says so itself rather than leaving it to be misread, which is the behaviour worth recording.

=== AND IT NAMED WHAT IT STRUCTURALLY CANNOT SEE ===

"The TYPES that cross these boundaries. Every axis here is a property OF a boundary; a struct or message that travels through one is part of the contract and is invisible to this check. A real case: a provider's storage API returned a type owned by its text crate, and the consumer read all three fields while naming neither." That is the exact breakage class this pair is exposed to, and no axis above would catch it (`con:pairing-stops-at-the-boundary`).

=== WHAT THIS SETTLES AND WHAT IT DOES NOT ===

SETTLED: the PoC's unanswered half — "whether seam_report's contract comparison is any good" — is now answerable. It ran, it refused to overclaim, and it named its own blind spot. The mechanism works.

NOT SETTLED: whether the two designs AGREE, because they have not said enough to disagree. The cheapest next step is now the mirror of the last one: state payload_schema, error_model and operations on the five `req-dyno-*` interfaces. That is a morning's work and it is the only thing that makes this report say more than "nobody said".

📌 METHOD NOTE, recorded because it cost time: this analysis was largely RE-DERIVED before `dec:linked-repos-poc` was found. Anthony redirected — "if you search the linking of projects, this was already discussed in the past" — and the prior record was both earlier and sharper, including `fact:the-diamond-meets-at-dynographs-internals-not-its-interface`. SEARCH THE GRAPH FOR PRIOR CROSS-PROJECT WORK BEFORE RE-RUNNING THE ANALYSIS; this design has a two-week head start on anyone re-deriving it.
